speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of the skin; have you noticed if this jaundice appeared within the first 24 hours of birth?

REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_level

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin level is 7 mg/dL, which is elevated for a newborn. Has your baby been feeding well and urinating or having bowel movements regularly since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the jaundice began after 24 hours and your baby is 5 days old with normal urine and stool output, this is likely physiologic or breast-milk jaundice. REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_direct AND Bilirubin_indirect. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Breast Milk Jaundice. The clinical picture of a 5-day-old exclusively breastfed infant with indirect hyperbilirubinemia (6.4 mg/dL), normal stooling, and onset after day 2 is classic for this condition. I will recommend increasing breastfeeding frequency or temporary supplementation if levels continue to rise.
